tasks.short: Compose shots to achieve the director's intended effects

steps.what: Check the director's shot intent and relevant camera, lens, filter and lighting references
inputs: director-issued current shot brief
equipment-owner current lens, camera and filter references
outputs: checked shot intent and technical references

steps.what: Apply the technical aspects of light, lenses, film, filters and camera settings to the actual camera setup
inputs: checked shot intent and technical references
actual camera, scene, light and available equipment

steps.what: Compose and frame each shot and refine it against the effects sought by the director
inputs: operator-adjusted actual camera setup
actual scene and director's intended effect

tasks.design: Configure current shot and equipment references in the {DOCS} so the operator can find the applicable pages quickly. Camera setup, composition and framing remain human responses to the actual scene and the director's intent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant current equipment reference can interrupt setup when a particular technical question arises.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document indexing and version filters can reduce navigation without judging the image.
tasks.still_hard: Lighting, movement, composition and the desired effect depend on the actual scene.
tasks.human_edge: Read a performance and adjust framing to convey the director's intention.

ambition.what: No new creative authority or service is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-2 for shot brief and equipment document access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: versioned document indexes can make relevant camera and lens references easier to locate.

assumptions: Boundary is the stated composition and framing work, including reference checks and actual setup. Recording a take, editing and distribution are separate tasks and yield no saving here.

Directors supply the current shot brief; equipment owners supply document id, version and equipment category. Missing metadata and interpretation stay in s1; no free scene analysis or automatic camera adjustment is assumed.
Native configuration first. This scenario includes occasional reference lookup rather than an invented report or settings log. No persistent record write or send is proposed.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Physical setup and creative work stay fully retained. If references are already immediately available or known, lookup saving is zero.
unknowns: Actual frequency of technical reference lookup
research_questions: Does the index reduce a real equipment-reference lookup without obscuring version applicability?
Is lookup material enough to justify upkeep?

incremental.description: Maintain equipment-reference categories and current-version links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 5 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 4.5. High allows 1.5 extra hours resolving reference exceptions; low applies when no repeated lookup remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with the production crew about filming requirements

steps.what: Review the current assignment, shot sequence and available production references before the crew discussion
inputs: production-owner current assignment and shot-list versions
existing crew and equipment references

steps.what: Confer with directors, sound and lighting technicians, electricians and other crew members about assignments, filming sequences, desired effects, camera movements and lighting requirements
inputs: checked filming discussion references
actual crew constraints, intentions and questions
outputs: actual filming decisions, requirements and open coordination issues

steps.what: Record actual sequence, camera movement, effect and lighting clarifications with their owners and unresolved questions
inputs: actual filming decisions, requirements and open coordination issues
checked filming discussion references

steps.what: Check attribution and meaning and approve the exact final filming clarification note
inputs: complete filming clarification note

steps.what: Save the approved note in the same internal production record
inputs: approved filming clarification note v1

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} discussion view to link current shot references from the {DOCS}, and reuse shot and assignment identifiers in the clarification note. The operator holds the actual crew conversation and records its decisions and uncertainties before checking and saving the approved note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding current production references and repeating known identifiers can add work around crew coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and forms can reuse shot references without inventing a transcript or crew consensus.
tasks.still_hard: Creative intent and physical production constraints need negotiation among the people doing the work.
tasks.human_edge: Expose a conflict between the intended camera move and actual lighting or sound needs.

ambition.what: No additional production authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for production documents and consultation if conversation records change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: production work views can link versioned shot lists and reuse identifiers in clarification forms.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference preparation, actual crew discussion and its existing written clarification note. Other crew time remains outside the focal denominator and receives no saving.

Production owners supply assignment id, shot id and current versions. s1 checks those references; s3 retains 10.5 hours for substantive decision, attribution and uncertainty capture. No free transcript or structured meeting output is assumed.
Native configuration first. The scenario assumes written clarifications already occur; if absent, remove the record component and remeasure rather than inventing paperwork savings.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system save remains fully retained; no automatic crew notification or new filming instruction is hidden in the design.
unknowns: Current production reference links and note practices
research_questions: Can the note distinguish a crew decision from an unresolved question?
Do linked current shot references reduce real preparation effort?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual filming clarifications and attribution

incremental.description: Maintain production-reference links and note fields

approvals.approved_version: approved filming clarification note v1; edits require s4 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 10.5 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 10. High allows three extra hours checking changed shot references; low applies where the native linked view and note already exist.

tasks.short: Edit video and prepare a checked broadcast-production handoff

steps.what: Interpret the broadcast production brief, intended story and technical delivery requirements
inputs: producer-issued current edit brief and delivery specification

steps.what: Locate and inspect the relevant footage and sound in the non-linear editing project's media bins
inputs: operator-understood edit and delivery requirements
existing ingest-produced media ids, timecodes and shoot metadata with actual source clips

steps.what: Edit video for the broadcast production using non-linear editing to choose shots, shape timing and make picture and sound cuts
inputs: operator-checked candidate source clips
operator-understood edit and delivery requirements
outputs: operator-authored complete picture and sound timeline

steps.what: Set the required technical delivery format and render a draft output from the completed timeline
inputs: operator-authored complete picture and sound timeline
producer-issued current edit brief and delivery specification
outputs: complete rendered draft output tied to the timeline version

steps.what: Watch and listen to the actual rendered output, resolve edit or technical issues and complete the internal handoff packet and recipient
inputs: complete rendered draft output tied to the timeline version
operator-understood edit and delivery requirements
producer-supplied internal handoff destination
outputs: complete checked edit project and rendered-media handoff packet

steps.what: Approve the exact final edit project, rendered output and internal recipient after all corrections
inputs: complete checked edit project and rendered-media handoff packet
outputs: approved internal edit handoff packet v1

steps.what: Save the approved final edit project version in its existing production project record
inputs: approved internal edit handoff packet v1

steps.what: Deliver the exact approved rendered output to the named internal production recipient
inputs: approved internal edit handoff packet v1
stored approved edit project version

tasks.design: Configure media-bin filters and validated delivery presets in the {OTHER} non-linear editing system. The operator finds clips more directly, makes all creative cuts, checks the actual rendered output and approves the finished project and exact internal handoff before separate save and delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated media navigation and delivery-setting entry can consume effort around creative editing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native bins and export presets can reuse existing metadata and fixed technical requirements without choosing the story.
tasks.still_hard: Story meaning, timing and subtle picture or sound faults require creative and perceptual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically valid cut changes meaning or weakens the intended story.

ambition.what: No new editorial or broadcast-release authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for source media and delivery specifications; review permitted footage access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: non-linear editing systems provide media-bin filters and reusable technical export presets.

assumptions: Boundary includes editing, technical draft rendering, quality review and an internal production handoff. Actual on-air broadcast or public publication is separate and receives no claimed saving.

Ingest staff already supply clip id, timecode and available shoot metadata. s2 retains watching and checking clips; missing metadata is handled manually rather than freely generated. No automatic transcript or semantic culling is assumed.

Producer supplies versioned delivery requirements and an internal destination. s4 reduces human setting entry and checking through presets, never render runtime. s5 retains full viewing, listening, corrections and rechecks; any changed timeline is rendered and reviewed again before s6.

Native configuration first. Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system save and short internal delivery stay fully retained; no automated publication is hidden in the design.
unknowns: Existing media metadata and preset use
research_questions: Can a preset reproduce the current delivery specification without hidden overrides?
Do media filters reduce navigation while retaining full clip judgement?

incremental.description: Maintain media filters and delivery preset versions

approved internal edit handoff packet v1 including rendered media and internal recipient; changes void approval

tasks.short: Instruct camera operators on setups and filming cues

steps.what: Review the current shot plan, camera assignments and director's intended movements and cues
inputs: director-issued current shot requirements
production-owner camera assignments and shot identifiers

steps.what: Determine camera setups, angles, distances, movement and variables and cues for starting and stopping filming
inputs: checked camera instruction references
actual scene and camera positions
outputs: operator-authored complete camera setup and cue choices

steps.what: Prepare the complete camera instruction and cue sheet with exact assigned camera operators
inputs: operator-authored complete camera setup and cue choices
checked camera instruction references
outputs: complete camera instruction and cue sheet with recipients

steps.what: Check and approve the exact final setup instructions, cues and assigned operator recipients
inputs: complete camera instruction and cue sheet with recipients

steps.what: Save the approved camera instruction sheet in the same production document record
inputs: approved camera instruction packet v1

steps.what: Instruct camera operators personally on the approved setups, angles, distances, movement and start/stop filming cues
inputs: approved camera instruction packet v1
actual assigned camera operators
outputs: actual camera instructions delivered and operator questions

steps.what: Check understanding through actual camera rehearsal and clarify any mismatch before filming
inputs: actual camera instructions delivered and operator questions
actual camera rehearsal and operator responses
outputs: checked operator understanding or revised instruction need

tasks.design: Configure shot-reference links in the {PROJECT} and a camera instruction layout in the {DOCS}. The operator determines and records actual setups and cues, approves the complete sheet and assigned recipients, then gives personal instructions and checks understanding in rehearsal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated shot identifiers and cue-sheet layout can add effort around the actual camera decisions and instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and fixed cue-sheet fields can reuse known references without deciding camera movements.
tasks.still_hard: A written cue does not show whether an operator understands the timing or can execute the movement.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt the instruction to the actual operator, camera position and rehearsal result.

ambition.what: No broader directing authority is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed camera cue-sheet layouts can reuse assigned shot and camera identifiers while people specify the actual movement and cues.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation, existing cue-sheet capture, live instruction and actual rehearsal confirmation. Other camera operators' rehearsal and filming time remain outside the focal denominator and receive no saving.

Directors supply current intent; production owners supply shot id and camera assignments. The focal operator forms actual setups and cues in s2 and captures them in s3; no free structured instruction or transcript is assumed.

s3 retains seven hours for actual cue entry and checking; only known references and layout change. Native configuration first. If no cue sheet is normally written, remeasure the live-instruction workflow instead of inventing paperwork savings.

The live instruction gate is the instructing operator's own final check of an already completed packet. Any changed cue, movement or recipient returns to s3/s4 before further transmission; software issues no live cue automatically.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system save and all instruction/rehearsal time remain fully retained.
unknowns: Existing cue-sheet practice and reference links
Actual effort in layout and identifier repetition
research_questions: Does the sheet retain all setup variables and cues after template assembly?
Can rehearsal reveal a mismatch that forces renewed instruction approval?

Keep cue instructions and recipients explicit
